support.meta.title: Support · Triple Peaks
support.meta.description: Help and support for Triple Peaks: FAQs, Strava connection, account, and data.
support.ph.h1: We're here to help you keep training.
support.ph.p: Answers to common questions, plus a direct line when you need one.
support.contact.h2: Drop us a line. We read every email.
support.contact.p: Bug, billing question, or feature idea. We typically reply within 24 hours on business days.
support.contact.note: For account deletion, billing issues, or anything you'd rather not ask in the app.
support.q1.body: Open the Triple Peaks app and go to Settings. Tap Connect Strava and authorize access. Your rides, runs, and swims will start syncing automatically, including GPS, heart rate, and power.
support.q2.body: To disconnect, revoke Triple Peaks' access in your Strava settings under "My Apps". Your synced data in Triple Peaks stays until you delete your account.
support.q3.body: Not officially yet. The iPhone app is on the App Store, and the Android app is in closed beta. Want in? Email triplepeaks@online.de and we'll send you a beta invite. In the meantime, the web app works on any device.
support.q4.summary: How do I manage my subscription?
support.q4.body: Subscriptions are managed through the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android). Open your device's subscription settings to change or cancel your plan. Your training history stays safe either way.
support.q5.summary: How do I delete my account?
support.q5.body: Open Settings in the app and select Delete Account. Your account and data are removed from the app, and clear from our backups over time. You can also email triplepeaks@online.de to request deletion directly.
support.q6.body: Check that your Strava connection is active in Settings. Tap Sync Profile under the Strava section to trigger a manual sync. If it still fails, revoke access in Strava's app settings and reconnect from the Triple Peaks app. If the issue persists, email us and we'll dig in.
support.q7.summary: Do you use AI, and what happens to my data?
support.q7.body: Yes. AI coaching is the core of the app. To build your plans, analyses, and chat replies, we send your training data to an AI provider, with your name and email removed first, so it sees your training rather than who you are. The provider doesn't use that data to train its models, and you can delete your account and data at any time. The Privacy Policy has the short version of everything else.
support.q8.body: We take reasonable care: connections are encrypted, access is limited to what's needed to run the app, and we never sell your data. No app can promise perfect security, but we keep the moving parts few and use established providers. Full details live in our Privacy Policy.

hero.h1:
A plan that fits your life.
Race day, ready.
hero.lede: Tell it your race and how much time you have. It builds the plan and fixes it when your week goes sideways.
hero.alt_note: No card. First plan in 90 seconds.
hero.phone_alt: Triple Peaks Today screen with a plan adjustment
strip.2.small: the plan is rebuilt around you
moments.h2: Your watch doesn't know your race. This does.
moments.m1.p: The hard run moves to Wednesday. Today is 30 easy minutes. One tap, no lost week.
moments.m1.alt: Today screen: hard run moved to Wednesday after a short night
moments.m2.p: A finish forecast that updates after every session. Not a gut feeling after Sunday's long run.
moments.m2.alt: Goal screen with a finish-time forecast chart
moments.m3.h3: How much should I ease off?
moments.m3.p: Ask the coach. It knows your last four weeks and answers in plain words: lighter this week, two short race-pace efforts on Thursday.
moments.m3.alt: Coach chat about tapering in race week
how.h2: You talk to it like a coach. It answers like one.
how.lede: No zones, no FTP, no jargon. Plain questions, plain answers.
how.s1.you: Half marathon on 25 Oct. I can do four days, about five hours a week.
how.s1.coach: Done. Week 1: tempo on Tuesday, easy on Thursday, long run Saturday, bike Sunday. First session is tomorrow, 40 minutes.
how.s2.you: Why am I running slower than usual today?
how.s2.coach: On purpose. Easy days are what make Saturday's long run count. Go by feel: you should be able to hold a conversation.
how.s3.you: Work trip this week, I only managed one run.
how.s3.coach: No problem. Next week starts easier and builds back up. You're a bit behind plan, still fine for 25 Oct.
how.s3.h3: Next week adapts to last week.
costs.h2: Good coaching used to be expensive.
costs.lede: Your watch guesses. Other AI coaches expect you to know your numbers. A human coach is great, if you can afford one and get a spot.
